concept: UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API
summary: Source-anchored research for UI automation of menu bar apps XCUITest and Accessibility API. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: XCUITest and the Accessibility API (AXUIElement) are the same technology underneath; XCUITest is a restricted predefined layer. Raw AX use requires the host binary to be granted in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility before running. (medium confidence)
AX hierarchies can be wrong for NSHostingView-based UI; MacPaw uses a hit-test technique at coordinates to reach hidden layers. (low confidence)

Apple does not support the Accessibility APIs in sandboxed apps. In a sandboxed menu bar app AXIsProcessTrusted returns false, the prompt never appears, and the app cannot be added in System Settings; with the com.apple.security.accessibility entitlement AX calls can still fail with .cannotComplete. A DTS engineer called this behaviour correct, in both local and TestFlight builds. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

XCUITest can find a menu bar status item with app.menuBars.statusItems and click it; a launch test can assert existence with app.menuBars.statusItems.firstMatch without checking isHittable. (medium confidence)

Content of a SwiftUI MenuBarExtra(.window) popover is not reliably in the accessibility tree under XCUITest; the safe launch guarantee is that the status item exists. Workaround: a DEBUG-only launch hook that opens the target window deterministically, or an NSStatusItem with an NSMenu and button accessibility label. (medium confidence)

If Xcode runs fullscreen, the menu bar is hidden and the status item test fails with 'Element StatusItem ... is not hittable'. Leave fullscreen before the run, or post a CGEvent mouse move near the top edge to reveal the menu bar (a reported, self-described ugly workaround). (low confidence)

On macOS Sequoia and later, XCTest UI tests prompt for a password to enable UI automation before each run, blocking CI. The accepted forum fix is `automationmodetool enable-automationmode-without-authentication`; disabling SIP and editing TCC did not help. This is a user-to-user answer, not an Apple statement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

Sandbox-safe alternatives to AX window inspection (CGWindow list, ScreenCaptureKit) need Screen Recording consent; AppleEvents exceptions are temporary and unsuitable for App Store distribution. A network monitor should not add them for testing. (low confidence)
Headless CI use: a shared Xcode scheme lets xcodebuild test run the UI test target without opening Xcode; the runner/helper needs Accessibility consent on first use. (low confidence)
